threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘Stokey’ is a cute nickname instead of a sign you’ve got the drink culture all wrong. We call it 'Stoke Newington' for a reason!
Last night, someone brought a full drum kit on the 196. By the time we got to Stockwell, they had a whole jam session going on.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I walked past the record shop and heard a street musician playing the same obscure track I had on vinyl. Felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a tram rolling down the street, completely ignoring the traffic lights, while cyclists whiz by in their own anarchic lanes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays; they’ve got a backup route ready while newcomers just stand confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus while another passenger recited Shakespeare. Only in the TL can a ride feel like a live show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm lies in its hidden plazas and local tapas bars that echo with laughter, not just tourists.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still pull out a map in Plaça del Sol, while the rest of us just look for the nearest bar.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is a fancy place, but the locals just call it 'that station with all the pigeons.'
Caught a couple arguing about Jollof rice on the 59 last night. Turns out, he prefers rice from a spot in Peckham. The passion was real.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home once I spotted the old Turkish guy selling fresh gözleme from his cart at Sonnenallee every Sunday morning. The line tells you everything.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop where the butcher also serves craft beer. It’s the kind of quirky mix that makes late nights here feel uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can tell how bad the BART delays are just by the number of people lined up at the taco truck.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus the other day, five people got on with burritos. They just kept passing around a hot sauce bottle. Classic Mission vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals love the plaça, but most of us avoid it. Too noisy, too many selfies. We prefer our corner bars away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still carry a plastic map—locals just rely on their phones and the occasional paella recommendation.
